heading: EXT. FLOATING TEAHOUSE - LANTERN MARSH - DUSK

units.text: EXT. FLOATING TEAHOUSE - LANTERN MARSH - DUSK
A raft-house on stilts drifts between reeds, paper lanterns glowing.
Steam curls from a copper kettle.
Six figures sit around a low table, each cup full, each smile polite.

KAELITH (30s, silver-braided elf, green sash) pours for MOTHER ORVETH (70s, a gnarled herbalist with moss in her hair) while BRAM STONEFIST (40s, dwarf warrior, bandaged hand) tears a rice cake in two, young PIP THISTLEWICK (teens, apprentice thief) pockets a spoon, the scholar DOMINIQUE ASHVALE (50s, ink-stained fingers) turns the pages of a ledger, and the ferrywoman SUN-HEE (60s, bamboo hat) hums at the tiller without ever looking at the passengers.
A toast. To the road behind us.
units.name: KAELITH

units.text: There are six names in this book. We are six.
units.name: DOMINIQUE

units.text: It is dated a hundred years ago.
units.name: DOMINIQUE

units.text: Sun-Hee lifts her head and, for the first time, looks at each of them in turn.
Kaelith lowers her cup, Bram's hand drifts toward his axe, Pip freezes mid-pocket, Dominique closes the ledger softly, and Mother Orveth smiles the way a river smiles at a stone.
The ferry does not return. It only arrives.
units.name: SUN-HEE

units.text: The lanterns go out one by one, and the water beneath the raft is no longer water.
